He played [[college basketball]] for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] before being drafted 16th overall by the [[Phoenix Suns]] and traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. ==High school career== Smith attended [[Lakeview Centennial High School]], where he was coached by J. T. Locklear. He averaged 20.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game as a senior. Smith earned District 10-6A MVP honors and was voted the best dunker in the Dallas region by area coaches. Coming out of high school, Smith was a three-star recruit and chose Texas Tech over Arkansas, Georgia Tech, Kansas State, Memphis, Oregon, and Texas.{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball Signs Zhaire Smith to NLI|url=https://texastech.com/news/2017/4/13/mens-basketball-signs-zhaire-smith-to-nli.aspx|website=[[Texas Tech Red Raiders]]|access-date=May 1, 2018|date=April 13, 2017}} ==College career== In his freshman season at Texas Tech, he averaged 11.3 points and five rebounds per game. He was an honorable mention Big-12 selection and was named to the conference's All-Defensive team. Alongside [[Keenan Evans]], Smith led Texas Tech to the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament, where they lost to eventual champion [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].{{cite news|last1=Dawson|first1=Peter|title=Texas Tech's Zhaire Smith officially signs with Roc Nation Sports, loses college {{sic|elig|bility|nolink=y}}|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-tech/article210173459.html|access-date=May 1, 2018|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=April 30, 2018}} Smith had a career-high 21 points and to go along with eight rebounds, three steals and two assists in a February 7 win over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite news|last1=Silva|first1=Carlos|title=Smith nets career high 21 points, powers No. 7 Texas Tech to fifth straight win|url=http://www.lubbockonline.com/sports-red-raiders-mens-basketball/sports-red-raiders/sports/2018-02-07/smith-nets-career-high-21|access-date=May 1, 2018|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=February 7, 2018}} He flirted with a triple-double with 18 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a 69–66 victory in the Round of 32 of the NCAA Tournament versus [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], and posted several highlight-reel dunks.{{cite news|last1=Silva|first1=Carlos|title=Zhaire Smith puts on show for pro-Texas Tech crowd in Dallas|url=http://www.lubbockonline.com/sports/20180318/zhaire-smith-puts-on-show-for-pro-texas-tech-crowd-in-dallas|access-date=May 1, 2018|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=March 18, 2018}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without initially hiring an agent.{{cite news|last1=Dauster|first1=Rob|title=Texas Tech star declares for draft without signing with agent|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/04/04/zhaire-smith-declare-nba-draft-texas-tech/|access-date=May 1, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 4, 2018}} In late April it was announced that Smith signed with Roc Nation Sports, thus ending his collegiate eligibility. ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2018–2020)=== On June 21, 2018, Smith was selected with the sixteenth overall pick by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]], but was immediately traded, along with the [[Miami Heat]]'s 2021 first-round pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for [[Mikal Bridges]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/smith-shamet-acquired-first-round|title=Draft 2018 Sought-After Prospect, Future Pick Highlight Acquisitions|work=NBA.com|first=Brian|last=Seltzer|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 22, 2018}} On July 2, he signed with the 76ers.{{cite web |title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Zhaire Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-sign-zhaire-smith |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 3, 2018 |language=en |date=July 2, 2018}} Head coach [[Brett Brown]] compared Smith to [[Kawhi Leonard]], who he helped to develop on the [[San Antonio Spurs]], as having played power forward in college and wanting to mold him into a wing player in a similar vein.{{cite web | url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2018/06/22/sixers-brett-brown-compares-zhaire-smith-kawhi-leonard-nba-draft-quotes/ | title=Zhaire Smith: Brett Brown 'compared me to Kawhi Leonard' | date=June 22, 2018 }}{{cite web | url=https://973espn.com/brett-brown-sees-kawhi-leonard-in-zhaire-smith/ | title=Brett Brown sees Kawhi Leonard in Zhaire Smith | date=June 22, 2018 }}{{cite web | url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/why-brett-brown-believes-in-high-flying-zhaire-smith/328726/ | title=Why Brett Brown believes in high-flying Zhaire Smith | date=June 22, 2018 }} Smith expressed to reporters that he wore #2 because Leonard was his favorite player.{{cite web | url=https://news4sanantonio.com/sports/spurs-zone/sixers-zhaire-smith-wears-no-2-in-honor-of-kawhi-leonard | title=Sixers' Zhaire Smith wore No. 2 in honor of Kawhi Leonard | date=June 25, 2018 }} On August 6, Smith fractured his foot at a summer development camp and required surgery.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=76ers rookie Zhaire Smith fractures foot at summer development camp and will need surgery, a report says |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/76ers-rookie-zhaire-smith-fractures-foot-at-summer-development-camp-and-will-need-surgery-a-report-says/ |access-date=August 7, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=August 7, 2018}} On August 10, 2018, the surgery to repair an acute Jones fracture of the fifth metatarsal in Smith's left foot was successful.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/medical-update-smiths-surgery-successful|title=Medical Update Smith's Surgery Successful|work=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2018|access-date=August 10, 2018}} Just one month later, in September 2018, Smith suffered a nearly fatal allergic reaction after eating Thai Chicken containing sesame. The episode was severe, requiring Smith to be hospitalized and placed on a feeding tube for nearly six weeks, ultimately losing over sixty pounds and a much of his overall strength.{{Cite web |date=2023-10-07 |title=Zhaire Smith's food allergy story is harrowing |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/zhaire-smiths-food-allergy-story-is-harrowing |access-date=2026-03-26 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}} While general manager [[Elton Brand]] expressed doubt that he would be able to play for the 76ers in the regular season, Smith opted to remake his jump shot in order to temporarily compensate for his much lower body strength. After successfully doing so, he made his debut with the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] for the [[NBA G League]] on March 1, 2019, against the [[Maine Red Claws]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/after-long-journey-court-zhaire-smith-makes-his-professional-debut-for-delaware-blue-coats-observations|title=After long journey back to court, rusty Zhaire Smith makes pro debut|first=Noah|last=Levick|date=1 March 2019|website=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]]}} He averaged 7.2 points with 3.0 rebounds and 1.5 assists in 11 G-League games with the Blue Coats, starting five.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/gleague/players/s/smithzh01d.html|title=Zhaire Smith G-League Stats|website=[[Basketball-Reference.com]]|access-date=April 24, 2019}} Smith made his NBA debut on March 25, 2019, in a 119–98 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]], scoring three points with a steal and one rebound in five and a half minutes of play.{{cite web|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/25/zhaire-smith-makes-long-awaited-nba-debut-in-blowout-loss-to-magic/|title=Zhaire Smith makes long awaited NBA debut in blowout loss to Magic|first=Ky|last=Carlin|website=Sixers Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=March 25, 2019|access-date=April 15, 2019}} In his rookie season, Smith averaged 6.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 18.5 minutes played in six games (two starts) including 17 points, four rebounds and five assists when he started the final game of the regular season against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://thesixersense.com/2019/04/12/philadelphia-76ers-rookie-report-zhaire-smith-starts/|title=Philadelphia 76ers Rookie Report: Zhaire Smith starts|first=Lucas|last=Johnson|website=TheSixerSense.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]|date=April 12, 2019|access-date=April 24, 2019}} Smith also played in two games during the [[2019 NBA Playoffs]] with the 76ers, albeit with limited production in either game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithzh01/gamelog/2019/ Zhaire Smith 2018-19 Game Log] On February 27, 2020, Smith had 16 points and six rebounds, shooting 7-for-16 from the floor in a 125–106 loss to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].{{cite news |last1=Carlin |first1=Ky |title=Sixers prospect Zhaire Smith beginning to show progress in G League |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2020/02/28/sixers-prospect-zhaire-smith-beginning-to-show-progress-in-g-league/ |access-date=March 2, 2020 |work=Sixers Wire |date=February 28, 2020}} On November 23, 2020, Smith was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Tony Bradley (basketball)|Tony Bradley]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-zhaire-smith-philadelphia-76ers|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Zhaire Smith From Philadelphia 76ers|work=NBA.com|date=November 23, 2020|access-date=November 25, 2020}} On November 30, Smith was waived by the Pistons.{{cite web|title=Zhaire Smith: Officially waived by Detroit|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/zhaire-smith-officially-waived-by-detroit/|website=CBS Sports|date=November 30, 2020|access-date=December 1, 2020}} On December 15, 2020, Smith signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]],{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Zhaire Smith and Bennie Boatwright|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-zhaire-smith-and-bennie-boatwright-201215|website=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2020|access-date=December 16, 2020}} but was waived the next day.{{cite news|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Christian Vital|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-christian-vital-201216|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2020|access-date=January 26, 2021}} Smith was included in the roster of the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]] in 2021 but did not play a game for the team.{{cite web|first=Sean|last=Barnard|title=Former Sixers' first-round pick Zhaire Smith making basketball comeback|url=https://phillysportsnetwork.com/2022/05/25/zhaire-smith-return-basketball/|website=PhillySportsNetwork.com|date=May 25, 2022|access-date=September 13, 2022}} ===Cleveland Charge (2023–2025)=== In July 2023, Smith joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]]{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=3 observations after Sixers fall short of massive comeback, finish Salt Lake summer league|url=https://www.nbcsportsphiladelphia.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/sixers-thunder-summer-league-observations-jaden-springer-zhaire-smith/527526/|website=NBCSportsPhiladelphia.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 7, 2023}} and on September 15, 2023, Smith signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Cavaliers Sign Zhaire Smith To Exhibit 10 Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/09/cavaliers-zhaire-smith-agree-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 15, 2023|access-date=September 15, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 21,{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Cavaliers Waive Seven Players|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/10/cavaliers-waive-seven-players.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} and one week later signed with the [[Cleveland Charge]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2023 Training Camp Roster|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2023-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=October 30, 2023}} On February 11, 2024, Smith signed a 10-day contract with the Cavaliers,{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Zhaire Smith to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/cavaliers-sign-zhaire-smith-to-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=February 11, 2024|access-date=February 11, 2024}} but didn't play for them. On February 23, he returned to the Charge.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Cleveland Charge Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Cleveland-Charge/34/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=February 23, 2024}} On September 24, 2024, Smith signed with the Cavaliers,{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Cavaliers Sign Jacob Gilyard, Zhaire Smith|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/cavaliers-to-sign-jacob-gilyard-zhaire-smith.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=September 25, 2024|access-date=September 25, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/releases-roster-update-241019|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 26, he joined the Charge.{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2024 Training Camp
